answer: Resistance uses a bonded identity kernel: an agent locks real stake to mint one vertex in the trust graph, and that vertex counts only if two unrelated existing vertices vouch for it. A violet receipt records the human who funded the bond and cannot be transferred. To flood the graph a Sybil farmer must buy fresh stake plus two genuine vouches for every fake vertex, so the attack cost rises with the square of identities while an honest agent pays only once.
